- **Docker image** — a `Dockerfile` with Chromium and its driver included (Intel/AMD and ARM), running as a non-root user with all data in `/data`. `docker-compose.yml` adds the API server and MongoDB. A new workflow builds the image on every push and pull request, starts Chrome inside it with the network off, and publishes version tags to `ghcr.io/georgekhananaev/google-reviews-scraper-pro`. The container runs signed out, so Google's 5-review wall applies there; see the README.

### Added
- **Sign-in expiry shows up in health checks** — `/health/scrape` gains `browser_profile` (`signed_in`, `signed_out`, `unknown` while Chrome holds the profile, or `not_configured`) and reports at least `degraded` when the profile is signed out, since every scrape then gets the capped list. `python start.py health` prints the profile state and says `DEGRADED` when it's signed out. `browser-login --check` says when the profile can't be read because Chrome is using it, instead of reporting it as si

- **No images saved on Windows** (PR #31 by @johntranb) — every place id contains `:` (`0x…:0`, `cid:`, `short:`, `hash:`), which Windows rejects in a folder name, so the images task failed with `WinError 123` and wrote nothing. Per-place image folders now use `_` instead of `:` on every OS (`review_images/0x30e29edb0244829f_0/`), in both the image task and the S3 task.
